newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's "Judge of the Year" accused of terrorism.
newsitem.headline: Peru's "Judge of the Year" accused of terrorism.

text.p: Peru's 1996 "Judge of the Year" is to face trial for terrorism after freeing a woman detained by police as a suspected leftist guerrilla supporter.

The government accused Elba Minaya Calle on Wednesday of "illegal behavior" and an "arrogant attitude" for ordering the woman's release from a Lima police station in June prior to the 15-day statutory limit for questioning guerrilla suspects.
An Interior Ministry ruling added that a state prosecutor had been named to press charges of terrorism, violence and abuse of authority against the judge.
Minaya told reporters, however, that she had merely "done my duty as a judge" in freeing someone unfairly held due to "an incorrect intervention by the police."

She added: "The constitution is above the terrorism law. It says that a person can only be detained in two cases, flagrant crime or judicial mandate. In this case, there was none of those two situations."
The prestigious Lima Chamber of Lawyers voted Minaya Judge of the Year in 1996 after she won notoriety for ordering the release from jail of outspoken retired military general Rodolfo Robles.
Peru's draconian anti-subversive legislation stipulates harsh sentences, including life imprisionment in the most serious cases, for terrorism convictions.
